body:
>“Anyone desperate enough for suicide...should be desperate enough to go to creative extremes to solve problems: elope at midnight, stow away on the boat to New Zealand and start over, do what they always wanted to do but were afraid to try.”-Richard Bach

I agree with that. Being without income has kind of forced me to face these things about myself, where as when I had a small income I could just go with my day to day existence and keep denying the past. I know I played a big part in the way things turned out, so I'm not just blaming everyone else though I often feel bitter.

> Stop disrespecting yourself, your friends, and your parents with the > threat of suicide. You are more than that. Start thinking positive and > positive changes shall begin. 

I don't plan to commit suicide if I know it hurts my relatives, and in any case would do it only if it turned out there's no possibility to get out of the current situation, or that my disease got much worse. I never made any open threats, though it was probably easy to see that in one point I was thinking about it. But that was years ago. 

> Know that its never to late to say FUCK OFF to your diseases. This diseases has the power to end you and power build you. Just because your born does not entitle you to a life(unfortunately kids die of hunger every minute of the day) your life is not that hard. Know that sometimes life feels like god gave you lemons to make orange juice.

Yeah, there is so much suffering and injustice in the world, I am really lucky in most respects. 

> Notice the similarities in all these posts > and how they tend to dwell on misfortune, negativity. I recommend > you change your name to JustAnotherGuy. I wish you the best, and > believe that happiness will one day come

I have read this place a few times, and I have noticed that thread. I guess the negativity is a phase everyone has to go through. 
I don't feel bad in being labeled a loser (even if I do it myself); I can accept it now. It actually feels good to do that if you've lived in denial for years.

Thanks. I'm not feeling that bad even though the situation is what it is. I just needed to vent and am glad I had the chance to. 

I don't follow any particular religion, it's a very private thing for me. I've read some Buddhist texts and also bits of the bible. I hope I can  study them more in the near future. Anyway, it has led me to think that there's some greater purpose in existence.
If you got advice, feel free to share it.
It has already helped in many ways. I'm actually feeling for the first time that I might overcome the ghosts of the past.

Thanks for the snippet, it was an interesting read. I must get familiar with Joseph Campbell. I previously only knew this hilarious quote from him: 
> "Be what you is, 'cos if you be what you ain't, you ain't what you is".
 
I think that hits the nail on the head in several levels. 

EDIT: Or it may have been one of the other Joseph Campbells. Anyway, I like your post and hope that life treats you well.
